qa_pairs.question: How do you specify an interpreted User-Defined Function (UDF) for Ansys Fluent through a journal file?
qa_pairs.answer: To tell Ansys Fluent to interpret your User-Defined Function (UDF) at runtime, you need to add the command `define/user-defined/interpreted-functions "sampleudf.c" "cpp" 10000 no` to your journal file. This command should be placed before the commands that read or initialize your simulation's case/data files. Remember to replace `"sampleudf.c"` with the actual name of your UDF source file. This method applies whether the simulation is run in serial or parallel.

qa_pairs.question: What steps ensure an interpreted User-Defined Function (UDF) is properly found and controlled by a journal file when running Ansys Fluent jobs on a cluster?
qa_pairs.answer: To ensure that an interpreted User-Defined Function (UDF) is found in the same directory as the journal file and that the journal file commands are in full control, you should open your `.cas` file in the Fluent graphical user interface (GUI), remove any existing managed definitions, and then resave the file. This ensures that only the command in your journal file will manage the UDF during job execution.

qa_pairs.question: Is there a special requirement for using an interpreted User-Defined Function (UDF) in parallel Ansys Fluent jobs?
qa_pairs.answer: Yes, if you plan to use an interpreted User-Defined Function (UDF) with parallel Ansys Fluent jobs, it must be parallelized. Further details on how to parallelize UDFs can be found in the "Parallel Considerations" section of the Ansys Fluent Customization Manual.
